# Job Chapter 26 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 425v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/JOB_026_page_001.jpg

---

**26:1** And-answered Iyyov and-said:

**26:2** "How you-have-helped [azarta] [the one with] no power [lo koach]! [How] you-have-saved [hosha'ta] the-arm [zeroa] [that has] no strength [lo oz]!

**26:3** How you-have-counseled [ya'atsta] [the one with] no wisdom [lo chokmah]! And-sound-wisdom [tushiyyah] in-abundance [la-rov] you-have-made-known [hoda'ta]!

**26:4** To whom [et mi] have-you-declared [higgadta] words [millin]? And-whose breath [nishmat mi] has-come-forth [yats'ah] from-you?

**26:5** The-shades [ha-refa'im] tremble [yecholelu] beneath [mitachat] the-waters [mayim] and-their-inhabitants [veshokneihem].

**26:6** Naked [arom] [is] Sheol [she'ol] before-him [negdo], and-there-is-no covering [kesut] for-Abaddon [la-avaddon].

**26:7** He-stretches-out [noteh] the-north [tsafon] over emptiness [tohu]; he-hangs [toleh] the-earth [erets] upon nothing [beli mah].

**26:8** He-binds-up [tsorer] the-waters [mayim] in-his-clouds [be-avav]; and-the-cloud [anan] is-not torn [niv'qa] under-them [tachtam].

**26:9** He-covers [me'achaz] the-face of-the-throne [pnei khisseh]; he-spreads [parshez] upon-it his-cloud [anano].

**26:10** A-boundary [choq] he-has-drawn [chag] upon the-face of-the-waters [pnei mayim], to-the-limit [ad taklit] of-light [or] with-darkness [im choshekh].

**26:11** The-pillars of-heaven [ammudei shamayim] tremble [yerofafu] and-are-astonished [veyitmahu] at-his-rebuke [mi-ga'arato].

**26:12** By-his-power [be-kocho] he-stilled [raga] the-sea [ha-yam]; and-by-his-understanding [bi-tevunato] he-struck-down [machats] Rahav [rahav].

**26:13** By-his-breath [be-rucho] the-heavens [shamayim] are-fair [shifrah]; his-hand [yado] pierced [cholelah] the-fleeing serpent [nachash bariach].

**26:14** Behold, these [are] the-edges [qetsot] of-his-ways [derakav], and-how [mah] small [shemets] a-whisper [davar] we-hear [nishma] of-him! But-the-thunder [ra'am] of-his-might [gevurotav] — who can-understand [yitbonen]?"

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**vv.2-4 — Bitter sarcasm:** Job's reply to Bildad opens with withering irony. "What a great help you've been to the powerless!" The Hebrew drips with contempt — Bildad's six verses of cosmic theology have done nothing for Job.

**v.5 — "the shades tremble":** Hebrew *refa'im* — the dead in the underworld. Job claims even the netherworld shudders before God. This goes far beyond what Bildad said.

**v.7 — "he hangs the earth upon nothing":** *Beli mah* — literally "upon not-what." A remarkable cosmological statement: the earth is suspended in void. This anticipates modern cosmology more closely than any other ancient Near Eastern text.

**v.12 — "he struck down Rahab":** *Rahav* — the mythological sea monster of chaos (cf. Isa 51:9; Ps 89:10). Job freely uses mythological imagery to describe God's power, while insisting this power remains beyond human comprehension (v.14).

**v.14 — "the edges of his ways":** Job's conclusion is devastating: everything Bildad described is merely the "fringe" (*qetsot*) of God's power — a faint whisper. The real thunder is beyond all hearing. Job out-theologizes his theologian friend.

*— EMET*
